A former racing driver, he built Jordan Grand Prix from junior formulas into a four-time Grand Prix winner. The team introduced Michael Schumacher to Formula One, and Jordan later became a television analyst. He also assembled investments across property, sport, media and finance.

long_biography.plain_text:
Jordan Grand Prix made its Formula One debut in 1991 and became one of the championship's defining independent teams. Under Eddie Jordan, it won four races, finished third in the constructors' standings and gave Michael Schumacher his first Formula One start. The team's colourful identity reflected a founder skilled at securing sponsors and spotting driving talent.

Jordan's route to team ownership began with karting after a Bank of Ireland posting in Jersey. He progressed through Formula Ford, Formula Three and endurance racing before deciding that managing drivers offered a stronger future than driving himself. His junior team won in Formula Three and Formula 3000, providing the platform for the leap into Formula One. After Jordan sold the operation in 2005, the Silverstone organisation changed hands repeatedly and eventually became Aston Martin's works team.
